dataset_family: Patreon purchased by study authors, March snapshots 2018 2021 2024, single external affiliation; not new independent source vs creator-income-evidence.json
frame: Patreon creators above US$10 monthly with only one listed external social platform, or Patreon-only. Missing earnings sometimes statistically imputed.
source_academic: Strauss, Yang and Mazzucato, Industrial and Corporate Change, DOI 10.1093/icc/dtag044 (2026).
missingness_criteria: Creators with no Patreon account or <= US$10 monthly Patreon income excluded
Some creator earnings imputed by source study regression
Counts are monthly selected cross sections, not a stable birth cohort
Different social affiliations have different genre and audience mixes
Income is Patreon monthly gross revenue proxy, not native YouTube advertising or net creator wages
interpretation_limits: Annual March medians are descriptive for different observed creator samples; not individual income changes
2024 affiliation medians compare a common Patreon mechanism but cannot identify native platform recommendation causes
Category tails pooled across platforms, so never assert YouTube-only animation buyers have a specified income
Mean > median here documents sample right-skew and does not establish representative all-creator mean
